reuse.why: Holiday movement is added inside the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend that every adjusting caller already uses, but getDatesInRange's daily skip rewrites the non-working-day test instead of using the new isNonWorkingDay.

duplication.why: The 'weekend or in holidays' predicate exists as isNonWorkingDay in shared/schedules.ts and again inline in getDatesInRange, and schedule-template passes a skipWeekend flag while also keeping its own skipWeekend ternary around the call.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the weekend logic, though the daily-skip check stays in the server app.

scope.why: Focused on holidays; widening the lookaround windows (2 to 14 days, take heuristics) is related but uses unexplained magic numbers.

maintainability.why: A loop over isNonWorkingDay generalises the weekend rule well, but the predicate is not exported and is repeated, redundant flags and ternaries pile up at the template site, and the window sizes are guesses.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange in packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts writes d.isWeekend(date) || config.holidays?.includes(...) inline instead of using the shared non-working-day predicate.

disguised_duplication.where: The isNonWorkingDay predicate from shared/schedules.ts is restated inline in getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) with dayFromDate and optional chaining.

one_place.where: Holiday-as-weekend is defined in isNonWorkingDay/getDateWithSkippedWeekend (shared/schedules.ts) but the daily-skip path in getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) applies its own copy.
